source.title: NCSLPH Certified Drinking Water Commercial Laboratories
limitations: Transcribed all in-state (NC) rows from the NCSLPH ShowDWLabs commercial drinking-water list retrieved by POST on 6 September 2026 (47 laboratories). Out-of-state commercial labs on the same roster are omitted (86 total on the all-states commercial list).

The commercial list and lab detail pages do not state whether a laboratory accepts private-well / homeowner samples. NC DHHS private-well FAQs say existing well owners can contact their local health department or a state-certified commercial laboratory — that is guidance, not per-lab verification. accepts_private_well_samples is unknown on every commercial row; call first.

Verified private-well path: North Carolina State Laboratory of Public Health chemical analyses for homeowners only if submitted through the local health department (Environmental Inorganic Chemistry page). Documented in a verified card, not as a commercial-list row.
Websites are not printed on the ShowDWLabs list or DisplayDWLab contact block — website is null for every row.
County is not printed — county is null.
Charlotte Water – Environmental Lab Services appears on the commercial certified list and is kept as printed.
Certification analyte lists are summarized from DisplayDWLab sectionHeader blocks; long lists may be truncated with “…”. Prices are intentionally omitted.
Phone numbers normalized to (XXX) XXX-XXXX when 10 digits were present; otherwise kept as printed.

verified_private_well.name: North Carolina State Laboratory of Public Health (via local health department)
verified_private_well.path: Submit through local county health department Environmental Health program
verified_private_well.notes: NCSLPH Environmental Inorganic Chemistry states a private water system (homeowner) can obtain chemical analyses from this Laboratory only if the sample is submitted through the local health department. FAQs also note State Lab testing is scheduled through the local health department.
